hook: Ethiopia says the Queen of Sheba was theirs.

verse.translation: “…she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, someone greater than Solomon is here.”

story: In 1 Kings 10, the Queen of Sheba travels to Jerusalem with a caravan of spices, gold and precious stones, to test King Solomon with hard questions.
Historians still debate where Sheba was. Ethiopian tradition, written down in the Kebra Nagast, names her Makeda and says she bore Solomon a son, Menelik, Ethiopia's first king.
Ethiopia's emperors traced their line back to Menelik for centuries, down to the last emperor, Haile Selassie, in 1974.
meaning: Jesus held her up as an example: she crossed the world to hear wisdom, and someone greater than Solomon was coming. The Fast of the Prophets is the waiting for him.

sources.title: 1 Kings 10:1–13 and Matthew 12:42, World English Bible (public domain)
Kebra Nagast (The Glory of the Kings), Ethiopian tradition compiled in the 1300s

review.notes: Ask family or Memhir Senay whether they'd tell the Makeda story differently.
